To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phosphoinositide-3-kinase/ Akt pathway regulates the cell cycle progression of human leukemia cells through the cytoplasmic relocation of the cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor p27(Kip1) and the control of cyclin (D1) expression.

the PI3/Akt pathway regulates the cell cycle progression of the HL60 human leukemia cell line through the control of the localization of forkhead transcription factor and the expression of p27Kip, cyclin D1, pRb, cdk6, and cdk2 activities.

the PI3 kinase/Akt pathway is important in the control of cell cycle progression of the HL60 human leukemia cell line through multiple mechanisms involving the control of the FoxO family of transcription factors and of the cdk4/6 inhibitor p27KIP1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanism(s) by which the PI3K/ Akt pathway regulates cell cycle in HL60 leukemia cells
the identification of new molecular mechanisms involved in the control and regulation of the cell cycle of human leukemia cells.
the identification of new molecular targets of the PI3/Akt pathway and the elucidation of the mechanisms by which these targets control cell growth and survival of leukemia cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PI3/Akt axis regulates the expression and activity of cdk inhibitors and cyclins and, as a result, the cell cycle progression in HL60 cells.
the PI3/Akt pathway regulates the cell cycle of HL60 cells by multiple mechanisms involving the activation/inactivation of FoxO factors, which in turn control the expression of p27Kip and cyclin D1.

the PI3k/Akt pathway regulates the cell cycle progression of human leukemia cells by controlling the subcellular localization of the cdk-inhibitor p27Kip and by modulating the transcriptional activity of the cyclin D1 promoter through the forkhead transcription factor FoxO3a.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PI3k/Akt pathway is a major regulator of the cell cycle and apoptosis in HL60 leukemia cells.

the PI3k/Akt pathway regulates the cell cycle progression of human leukemia HL60 cells by controlling the expression and subcellular localization of FoxO transcription factors and the cdk inhibitor protein p27Kip-1.

in HL60 human leukemic cells, activation of the PI3k/Akt pathway results in a cell cycle progression through mechanisms involving the control of the FoxO1 and 3 transcription factors, the relocalization of p27Kip to the cytoplasmic compartment, and the hyperphosphorylation of the cdk4 and cdk6 inhibitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

PI3K/AKT pathway activation may promote cell cycle progression of human leukemia cells through multiple mechanisms involving the control of the forkhead transcription factors FoxO1 and/or FoxO3, the cdk inhibitor protein p27Kip, and cyclin D1.

the PI3k/Akt signaling pathway regulates the cell cycle progression of leukemia cells through mechanisms that include the cytoplasmic relocation of FoxO1, and FoxO3, the control of cyclinD1 and cdk6, and the phosphorylation of p27Kip.
in human leukemia cells, the PI3K/akt axis regulates cell cycle through multiple mechanisms involving the control of forkhead transcription factor and cdk inhibitor p2 7 Kip1.
